claimVerdicts.note: Abstract p1: level 4 case series, 100 male players, 97 followed at least 9 months, 84% RTC (100% pro, 80% amateur).
Abstract results p1; all ten percentages match.
Figure 3 caption p3: "gradual transition from rehabilitation to performance training along a continuum".
p8 key-points bullet; claim keeps the 'can be used to' modality.
Table p6, Q11 asks about criteria "to release athletes following HSI to return to training with the team"; all percentages match.
Digest p17 abstract of the editorial, verbatim. It concerns the 'deceleration index', a different construct from GPS deceleration distance.

212 abstract p1 and digest p6 match. The paper adds "observational study design precludes the examination of causal relationships" and later notes overlapping CIs between days; the brief carries the non-causal caveat.
p9: "this optimal chronic dose is likely specific to each population and context"; the dose refers to weekly exposure number, which the claim does not misstate.
683 abstract p1 verbatim, including rho and p values and the 58-player sample.

statementIssues.note: "Total distance plateaued, and the authors judged it not useful for progression decisions" is true (705 p6: "The plateau in TD suggests that it is not a useful metric for RTC decision-making or for progressing through OFR") but no claim carries this excerpt, so it is untraceable within the brief.
Same untraceable total-distance statement cited to C2/C3, which do not contain it; the source supports it at p6.
"Practitioners ... combined several criteria rather than one cutoff" is an inference from aggregate percentages; the survey does not report per-respondent combinations.
Presents rho -0.13 and -0.08 without saying these are very weak correlations, which limits their value as a monitoring basis.
D-2 placement option is caveated as retrospective and hamstring-only, but omits the authors' note that CIs between days overlap (p9).
Says 212 was used via digest abstract, but C9 and C10 cite the 212 PDF directly.

tierNote: Limited fits: no source tests a 7-10 day structure or hold/regress triggers; evidence is a level 4 case series, a single case, a retrospective association study, a survey and an editorial. No recommendation was issued; options are labeled as untested.
usefulnessNote: Gives PT and performance staff a concrete, accurately sourced way to plan the window (metric-by-metric gaps versus team-training and match references, deceleration as the largest gap, caveated near-max speed timing) and is explicit that hold/regress triggers and decision ownership are local judgment. It does not supply hold/regress criteria, but says clearly that the library cannot.
suggestedDrafterFixes: Every factual statement in bottomLine and actions must map to a claim whose excerpt contains it; add a claim rather than citing a neighbouring one.
Report effect-size context (for example 'very weak correlation') alongside raw statistics.
Keep sourceReview descriptions consistent with which document each claim actually cites.
Carry forward authors' own uncertainty statements (overlapping CIs) when presenting timing or dose options.
